findings.summary: The registry disagreed with itself: versions.json said 3.13.0 while the pin was 3.14.0.
findings.detail: Nothing in the tooling compared the version records, so the registry could hold a stale design-system version indefinitely without any signal. This produced the pin/cross-check design in protocol.md and the drift register in deep-check.md: a pin that is stated but never checked is not a pin.

findings.summary: Published tiles were citing internal workspace paths that mean nothing to anyone who clones the registry.
findings.detail: Introduced during the workspace reorganisation, then caught. The fix established a rule now in tile-format.md: provenance cites resolvable ground truth (package@version, live URL, observation date); process records live in the project workspace. A registry is a published artifact and must stand alone.

ECL: an allowlisted class was mistakenly treated as verification, stamping 61/61 instead of 49/61
findings.summary: An allowlist is a drift register, not a waiver — and a single prefix left whole namespaces unchecked.
findings.detail: Two mechanisms failed in the same session. First, verification accepted allowlisted classes as passing, so drifted tiles were stamped as verified until the predicate was corrected to test real definition. Second, GOV.UK and canada.ca span several class namespaces (govuk-/gem-/app-, wb-/btn-/form-/gc-) and a single prefix silently unchecked the rest. Both fixes are now in the spec, and the second one generalises the two-axis rule to multi-namespace registries.

round-trip-tests/
findings.summary: L2 — incomplete class metadata makes every class-level tool silently miss components.
findings.detail: 149 of 152 USWDS tiles lacked uswdClass, so a whole search family was invisible to the coverage checker. The other four registries had 100% coverage from day one because their builders emitted it. The lesson generalises beyond USWDS: a missing facet does not fail, it disappears, so coverage of the metadata is itself a checked property. Later generalised to the per-namespace classCheck prefixes (uswds:F-008).

evidence: task-usability/runs/t5-001 (2026-09-17): relative-only countdown ('ends in 12 days') persisted across turns 0-2 at high severity with CLEAN class coverage
task-usability/runs/t5-002: re-measured — resolved; the absolute date appears from turn 0

findings.summary: L11 — a closed loop: found in t5-001, fixed with a guidance flag, re-measured resolved in t5-002.
findings.detail: The most important thing about this finding is its shape, not its content. Class coverage was clean the whole time — the defect was that nothing in the metadata said a time-sensitive warning must state an absolute date. It is therefore not detectable by any class-level tool, only by a task test, which is why guidance flags exist as a separate mechanism. The re-measurement is what makes it evidence rather than a plausible fix: the same task was run again after the change and the finding did not recur.

residual (low severity, recorded in the run's PROVENANCE): name the checkout destination; state where to cancel; explain dismiss persistence
findings.summary: L12 — a closed loop: found in t5-001, fixed with refined guidance, re-measured in t5-003 with highs eliminated.
findings.detail: Same shape as F-011 and worth keeping adjacent to it: an agent can satisfy every class and structural rule and still produce an unusable experience, because nothing said the commitment action must state its consequence before the click. The refined guidance (cadence plus click consequence) is what took it from high to low, and the residuals are recorded rather than smoothed away — a closed loop is not the same as a perfect result.
